Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — observability / ops tooling comparison vs hyperscalers

Hi Jamie — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum.

Recap (what we covered)
- Primary goal: standardize inference across teams (hosted + dedicated) while lowering per-token cost and improving latency SLAs for user-facing features.
- Hyperscaler comparison focus: integration friction, monitoring/traceability, cold-start behavior, and unit economics for conversational workloads.
- Operational tooling: observability (per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns), tracing (end-to-end request traces + model route attribution), and usage analytics for budgeting/chargeback.

Redwood differentiators we discussed vs hyperscalers / other inference APIs:
- Unified API across hosted/dedicated/private deployments — same rollout controls and routes.
- Token-level cost + latency breakdown for every request (helps ops tune batching/quantization).
- Automatic prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching that preserves latency SLOs while reducing cost.
- Built-in rollouts (canary/A-B/fallback) and per-route tracing so you can correlate regressions to model changes quickly.

Proposed next tests (recommendation)
1) Latency & throughput baseline: 1k concurrent short-chat requests (avg 128 tokens) — compare Redwood Hosted vs Redwood Dedicated vs OpenAI/Vertex endpoints.
2) Observability check: validate that per-token cost and trace attribution appear in the dashboard for identical request sets.
3) Regression test: run your 50-sample prompts used for quality evals to ensure parity across model variants.

Attachments: I'll share a short benchmarking plan and our SOC2 summary (for procurement).

Next steps / asks for you
- Can you confirm which region you want testing in (us-west/us-east)?
- Can we get procurement looped in if you want SOC2 + pricing? (cc'd address is fine)
- Suggest 30–45 min follow-up next week to align on test matrix — what times look good?

Thanks — I’ll have Rishi & Vivek help with the benchmark plan and runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Vivek —
Putting an initial benchmark runbook together based on Marissa's notes. High-level plan attached. Key points:
- Test matrix: three endpoints (Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, OpenAI/Vertex) x two load profiles (burst 300rps short-chat; steady 1k concurrent low-latency).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens at observed rates, cold-start 95th percentile, and per-request trace id for correlating to dashboard.
- Observability validation: ensure every request surfaces model_id, route_id, cost_estimate, and KV-cache-hit in the trace metadata.

I attached redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf — please review and flag any scenarios we should add (e.g., long-context streaming tests).
